root_cause.text: In `libceph`’s `osdmap_decode()` the bounds check underestimates the size of the per-OSD `osd_weight` data, because `ceph_decode_need()` only reserved `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` ერთხელ even though `osd_state` and `osd_weight` are decoded in a loop `map->max_osd` times, allowing a corrupted OSD map to drive out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `ceph_decode_need(... + sizeof(*map->osd_weight), ...)` to `... + map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight), ...`, and the CVE text states that both `osd_state` and `osd_weight` are decoded for each OSD (`map->max_osd` times) but the check “only accounts for `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` once,” which can lead to OOB access if `max_osd` exceeds the actual message content.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the osds decode block. The code reserves space with `ceph_decode_need(p, end, 3*sizeof(u32) + map->max_osd*(1 + sizeof(*map->osd_weight) + sizeof(*map->osd_addr)), bad);` and then decodes `osd_state`, `osd_weight`, and `osd_addr` for `map->max_osd` entries. The root cause is the underestimation of per-OSD `osd_weight` data in the bounds check, and here the check only includes `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` once per entry, while the actual decode loop `for (i = 0; i < map->max_osd; i++) ceph_decode_32(p, map->osd_weight[i]);` shows the exact vulnerable read path. There is no additional corrective logic such as a larger per-entry reservation or separate bounds validation for the full loop, so the fix is not present in this function body.
